style: Hand-drawn Czech storybook illustration, like a classic Czech children's book illustrator working in ink and watercolor. A lively, irregular dark brown ink outline of varying thickness, slightly wobbly, drawn by hand around every shape including small details. Flat, slightly textured watercolor washes inside the outlines that spill a little over the line in places and stop short of it in others. Muted natural palette: sage green, olive, earthy clay brown, slate blue-grey, warm cream paper, dusty pastel pink and ochre; small rare accents of brick red and mustard yellow. Minimal shading: only a slightly darker wash and a few hatching strokes or squiggles instead of texture. No gradients, no glow, no bloom, no glossy highlights, no 3D render look, not vector flat design, no saturated candy colors. Characters are drawn simpler than the backgrounds.
notext: No text, letters, digits, numbers, signs, labels, captions, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image.
magenta: Background: one flat solid color, exactly pure magenta #FF00FF, covering the whole canvas edge to edge; no gradient, no texture, no floor, no cast shadow on the ground, no frame, no checkerboard pattern. Do not use magenta or bright pink anywhere inside the drawings.
grid: Square image divided into an invisible 2x2 grid of four equal cells (no lines drawn between them). Each cell holds exactly one subject, centered, filling about 70 percent of its cell, with clear magenta space around it so the four subjects never touch each other or the cell edges.

Three original characters of a family quiz show, each shown in three poses side by side (front view standing, three-quarter view gesturing, back or side view), clearly separated into three rows. Row 1, the main character: MADAM OWL, a plump tawny owl with soft brown and cream feathers, round amber eyes with small round wire glasses, wearing a hand-knitted sage green vest with a simple cream zigzag pattern and a small brick-red bow at the neck; she holds a few blank question cards; warm, a bit theatrical, friendly. Row 2: the scorekeeper, a cheerful long dachshund dog, reddish-brown, wearing a mustard yellow knitted scarf, holding a pencil and a blank notepad. Row 3: a small round house sparrow messenger, grey-brown, with a tiny slate blue knitted cap, carrying a small blank envelope. Keep anatomy simple and readable, big expressive eyes.

The SAME owl character MADAM OWL from the attached model sheet (tawny owl, round wire glasses, sage green knitted vest with cream zigzag, brick-red bow), full body, four poses: 1) top-left: waving hello with one wing, smiling; 2) top-right: holding up a blank question card, eyebrows raised, asking; 3) bottom-left: cheering with both wings up, tiny confetti of blank paper squares around; 4) bottom-right: thinking, wing tip at the beak, looking up.

Wide landscape illustration, 16:9. A cozy evening in an ordinary Czech family living room-kitchen, seen as a diorama from a gently elevated three-quarter view. Around it a family playing games: mother and father (adults in their thirties, sweater and flannel shirt), a schoolboy of about nine with a pencil writing on a sheet of paper, and a preschool girl of about five standing on her chair holding up a playing card triumphantly. On the table: scattered playing cards, sheets of paper, pencils, a teapot and mugs of tea, a jug of homemade raspberry lemonade, a bowl of crisps and a small plate of buchty buns. In the background: a tiled stove or radiator, a window with a dark blue evening sky and a panel block with a few lit windows, a kitchen cupboard, a houseplant, a cat sleeping on a chair. The owl MADAM OWL from the attached model sheet sits on top of the cupboard like a quiz host, holding a blank card; the dachshund from the sheet lies under the table. Humor in details. Composition: keep the upper-left third calm and fairly empty (wall and soft lamp light) as space for a title; the family and table on the right and center.

Landscape illustration, 4:3. A family plays the classic Czech board game Člověče, nezlob se (a cross-shaped race board game like ludo) on a big wooden kitchen table in the afternoon: the square board lies in the middle, a cross-shaped track of round spaces with four coloured corner home areas (muted sage green, slate blue, ochre yellow and brick red) and little wooden cone-shaped pawns in the same colours, one white wooden die with pips mid-roll on the board. A girl of about six shakes a die cup with both hands and squeals with excitement, her older brother pretends to be outraged because his pawn was just sent home, mum laughs with a hand over her mouth, grandma calmly counts spaces with her finger. The owl MADAM OWL from the attached model sheet sits on the edge of the table like a referee, holding up one wing. Details: a jug of raspberry syrup and glasses, a plate of poppy-seed buchty buns, a cat batting a fallen pawn on the floor, a kitchen dresser with plates and a window with geraniums. Diorama view slightly from above. The die shows only pips (dots), never digits.

pics: Picture-dictionary icons for a quiz for children aged three to six who cannot read yet. Each subject is ONE single, iconic, instantly recognizable thing shown whole, in its most typical view, with a big simple silhouette and a bold clear ink outline, drawn a little simpler and chunkier than usual, so that it reads at a glance even at a tiny thumbnail size. No background, no scenery, no ground, no extra props, no other objects, no frames. Animals look friendly and natural (not dressed), young animals are visibly babies: smaller, rounder, bigger heads and eyes. All four subjects share the same scale of detail and the same style. Wide subjects (animals in side view, vehicles) are drawn smaller, about 55 percent of the cell width, so that the WHOLE subject including head, snout, trunk, horns and tail stays well inside its own quarter with a clear magenta margin; nothing may touch or cross the vertical or horizontal middle line of the image.
